prerequisites: Students must have completed a general course on materials science in their previous Bachelor's degree.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the fundamental processes used for forming industrial parts, their characteristic defects, and how to reduce them.
Understand the different grades of carbon and alloy steels, their fundamental characteristics, and applications.
Understand the possibilities for modifying the mechanical properties of steels through microstructural changes generated by heat treatments.
Understand the fundamental characteristics of the main families of stainless steels, their advantages, and limitations.
Understand the various industrially available surface treatments for hardening the surface of metal parts.
Understand the fundamental parameters on which the properties of ferrous alloys depend and how to control them.
Understand the most important light alloys and their characteristic heat treatments.
Understand the most representative structural plastics, their characteristic forming processes, and their reinforcement mechanisms.
Understand the most representative structural ceramics, their characteristic forming processes, and available toughness enhancement mechanisms.
Identify the most suitable material for use in specific structural applications.
Design materials with better mechanical properties in order to produce novel products or products with better performance.
Design heat and surface treatments to improve the in-service behavior of specific parts and components.
Manage technical specifications and available standards on materials, their analysis, and testing.
Acquire the necessary skills, work methodology, and handling of laboratory equipment for characterizing structural materials.
Combine different characterization techniques to obtain detailed information on the materials under study and solve practical problems that may arise.
Encourage in the student a desire to acquire practical knowledge.
Lay the foundations for the student to be able to apply acquired knowledge in engineering.
Foster an open, critical, cooperative, and entrepreneurial spirit.

syllabus_topics: Manufacturing processes of metallic parts. Molding procedures. Rolling and forging processes. Hot and cold plastic forming. Forming from powders. Characterization of characteristic defects.
Carbon structural steels. Influence of carbon content on the mechanical properties of steels. Microalloyed steels and thermomechanical treatments. Types of low/medium strength construction steels.
Heat-treated steels. Austenite transformation curves. Heat treatments. Types of high/very high strength steels.
Tool steels. Steels for cold working. Steels for hot working. High-speed steels.
Stainless steels. Ferritic steels. Martensitic steels. Austenitic steels. Duplex steels. Advantages and disadvantages of the different families.
Surface heat treatments. Carburizing. Nitriding. Carbonitriding. Nitrocarburizing. Other surface treatments.
Ferrous castings. White cast irons. Gray cast irons. Graphite control and types. Heat treatments. Special cast irons.
Light alloys. Main alloys. Hardening methods. Characteristic heat treatments. Aluminum alloys. Magnesium alloys. Titanium alloys.
Plastics for engineering use. Types of structural plastics. Thermal and mechanical properties. Other properties. Reinforced plastics. Plastic part forming processes.
Ceramics for engineering use. Ceramic forming processes. Mechanical properties of ceramics. Technical ceramics.

Materials for extreme temperature applications. Low temperatures. Ductile-brittle transition temperature. Available materials. Materials for high-temperature applications. Creep and oxidation problems. Available materials.

assessment_methods.method: Group work reports, presentation, and debate
Theory and practical case resolution test

assessment_rules: The final grade is composed of 20% from submitted exercises and laboratory scripts, 20% from group work reports and presentations, and 60% from two evaluation sessions (30% for a written exercise test and 30% for a theory and practical case resolution test). A minimum of 4 points out of 10 is required for the combined written and theory evaluations to pass the course.
